title: `UNION`, `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT`, with and without `ALL`: NULLs equal
verdict: SQL's set operations; NULLs (and NaN, ±0.0) equal; no order
description: `UNION` deduplicates and `UNION ALL` keeps every row; `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` deduplicate; `INTERSECT ALL` keeps min(m, n) copies and `EXCEPT ALL` max(m - n, 0). NULLs compare equal, so do NaN and the two zeros. `UNION ALL` of two small inputs came back in input order; nothing guarantees it.
reference: `UNION ALL` is bag union and `UNION DISTINCT` its `distinct`; `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` are semi and anti joins with NULLs equal, then `DISTINCT`, and the `ALL` forms number equal rows (#344). Spark is native.

evidence.note: Set operators compare NULLs as equal

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
